title: Preparing for Employment Costs S. Koreans $440 a Month
paragraphs: Looking for a job can be tiring — and also very expensive!
According to a new survey, people in South Korea spend an average of 580,000 won — almost $440 — each month preparing for employment.
The survey was done by Mono Research for the Federation of Korean Industries. It included 1,000 people aged 19 to 34, all of whom were looking for work at the time of the survey.
It found that nearly 70% feel financially strained because they spend a lot of money doing things that will help them get a job.
Certifications and language tests are the top expenses, the survey found, followed by general education costs and study materials.
People who have been preparing for employment for three years or more were found to spend an average of 800,000 won, or about $600, each month.

The survey also found that older job seekers spend more than younger ones. Those aged 30 to 34 were found to spend an average of 600,000 won — about $450 — each month, while those aged 19 to 24 spend 560,000 won, or about $420.
People looking for work in education, medicine and health were found to spend the most on preparation. Those hoping to work for very large companies also spend more than the average.
The survey also found that 33% of participants get financial help from their families to cover these costs. Another 30% use money they get from part-time jobs or other work.
When asked what kind of support would help them most, a quarter said they want financial help with certification and language test costs.
Another 17% said housing support, including help paying rent, would be useful.
